look_here_first: KNOTROOT BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): FIRST verify a living short hard knotty basal rhizome, then a generally short even-width dense foxtail head (~3–8 cm). FNA reports 4–12 persistent bristles, 2–12 mm long, beneath each spikelet; they must be counted from a genuinely intact head at 10–20×. Our only stored macro shows green bracts and pink emergent floral tissue with a 2-mm scale, NOT the perennial rhizome or a countable group of 4–12 basal bristles.
photo_note: 2026-10-21: original physical JPEG inspected; visible structures annotated without manufacturing bristle attachment. Other three original-photo comparisons credited. One photo per taxon is a field cue, not diagnostic closeout.
identification_caution: Source-labelled Croatian 2-mm macro does NOT document Texas locality, species-critical hard rhizomes, or a safely countable set of subtending bristles; identify under multi-character field key.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Distinguish from annual yellow foxtail S. pumila and green foxtail S. viridis using actual knotty perennial rhizomes; neither is a canonical species here. S. reverchonii has longer interrupted heads with bristles much sparser, S. scheelei has usually one very long conspicuous projecting bristle and longer loose/tapered head. Foxtail millet S. italica is cultivated/escaped annual; its dense head alone is insufficient.
diagnostic_sequence: Inspect the basal rootstock for short hard knotty rhizomes; do not uproot protected or sensitive plants.
Use a hand lens on spikelets: several bristles at each base; spikelets approximately 2–3 mm.
Photograph leaf ligule and a complete plant habit; existing single macro does not show the decisive rhizome.
not_reliable_alone: Color or texture of seedhead without bristle group macro
Bristles mistaken for true floret awns or flower stigmas
Mature spikelet counts read from a photo too small to show attachment
Cultivated or habitat context presented as confirmed local nativity

best_field_traits: KNOTROOT BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): FIRST verify a living short hard knotty basal rhizome, then a generally short even-width dense foxtail head (~3–8 cm). FNA reports 4–12 persistent bristles, 2–12 mm long, beneath each spikelet; they must be counted from a genuinely intact head at 10–20×. Our only stored macro shows green bracts and pink emergent floral tissue with a 2-mm scale, NOT the perennial rhizome or a countable group of 4–12 basal bristles.
Perennial with firm short knotty rhizomes, to about 4 cm in a local Texas botanical treatment, sometimes with swollen buds at shoot bases.
Stem nodes often bent (geniculate); short densely bristly cylindrical flowering heads commonly 25–70 mm.
Many sterile bristles grouped beneath each spikelet: usually six or seven, observed local-treatment range about four to twelve.
Spikelets about 2.2–2.5 mm long; no floret awns (bristles are sterile reduced branchlets).
Thin blades frequently about 2–4.5 mm broad, with a mixed membranous/hairy true ligule roughly 0.5–1.3 mm.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Complete short densely bristly terminal head with ruler and multiple intact spikelet bases
Rooted same-plant hard knotty rhizomes with buds and centimeter ruler (only where collection legal)
True 4–12 basal persistent bristles clearly separable from exserted flower parts (10–20×)
Intact 2–2.8 mm ripe spikelet, glumes/upper lemma, and hair-like ligule
crew_field_check: First find the WHOLE panicle and compare crowded/loose head arrangement without forcing species from silhouette.
Inspect an intact attached SPIKELET at 10–20×. Count the SUBTENDING PERSISTENT BRISTLES (sterile branches), not grass awns or protruding flower parts.
Record bristle count/length and spikelet length using a 1-mm scale, and compare the same-plant collar ligule.
Check a rooted base only where collecting is legal: annual fibrous millet vs knotty rhizomatous perennial parviflora/reverchonii, and perennial scheelei.
Existing archival images do not prove every underlying bristle count or rhizome; if unresolved identify Setaria sp.

visual_comparison.memory_rule: MILLET=ANNUAL HEAVY HEAD (usually 1–3 bristles); PARVIFLORA=KNOTTY RHIZOME + MANY (4–12); REVERCHONII=INTERRUPTED SPARSE (2–8 mm where bristled); SCHEELEI=LONG SINGLE (10–35 mm).

items.label: Foxtail millet — dense, nodding cultivated seedheads
items.image_role: Real existing garden/crop overview showing branching millet head silhouette rather than microscopic identity
items.caption: Original credited overview shows multiple long densely packed, at times curved and drooping foxtail-millet heads with relatively wide leaves. It cannot expose individual basal bristle counts, ligules, exact millimeters or true annual root system.
items.why_it_matters: FOXTAIL MILLET (INTRODUCED annual crop/escape): start with stout annual culms, broad foliage, and a heavy dense often lobed or nodding foxtail head. Flora of North America usually describes 1–3 persistent subtending bristles (to ~12 mm), NOT 'numerous bristles beneath every spikelet'. A crop-derived head varies greatly; distinguish from perennial native bristlegrasses using rooted duration, panicle shape and ripe spikelets.

items.label: Reverchon's bristlegrass — interrupted slender panicle
items.image_role: Existing Texas source-labelled photo for sparse panicle architecture, not measured bristle anatomy
items.caption: Eric Knight's photo shows a narrow vertical seedhead with separated, sparse clusters of green spikelets. The finger is only an informal size cue. The tiny spikelet bases do not resolve the number or exact length of persistent bristles.
items.why_it_matters: REVERCHON'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): the existing real photo shows a skinny, often interrupted upright flowering head, with widely separated spikelet groupings. Its bristles are sparse—some spikelets appear almost unbristled—but FNA gives bristles about 2–8 mm where present; do NOT teach a hard ≤2 mm cutoff. Seek short knotty rhizomes, the stiff hair ligule (1–2 mm), and mature 2.1–4.5 mm spikelets. No bristle measurement is visible in the original picture.

items.label: Southwestern bristlegrass — long projecting bristles
items.image_role: Existing exact-source flowering photograph: conspicuous long bristles and spikelet-bearing axis visible
items.caption: Kyla Miller's source photo clearly shows a long tapered green flowering axis, many ovoid pale spikelets and conspicuously long, outward-pointing bristles. The photo does not itself prove each bristle belongs to just one spikelet or provide a measurement ruler.
items.why_it_matters: SOUTHWESTERN / SCHEELE'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): a tall, commonly broad-leaved and hairy grass with a long, tapered, rather open bottlebrush-like head. Usually 1 (sometimes 2–3) LONG separate projecting bristles per spikelet, typically 10–35 mm in FNA/Kew. Unlike Reverchon's shorter sparse bristles, these long bristles are actually obvious in the saved flowering photograph. Edwards Plateau shady limestone canyon habitat is supportive, not conclusive.
